Yes. 0.999... is the limit of the sequence 0.9, 0.99, 0.999, ..., which is exactly 1. Their difference is smaller than every positive number, so it is 0.

Quick check: let x = 0.999...; then 10x = 9.999..., so 9x = 9 and x = 1. (This relies on the standard real-number arithmetic that defines the repeating decimal as a limit.)
